snapshot_note: Snapshot as of 2026-09-28. Cells come from each tool's own docs/posts at the dates shown; not re-verified beyond that pass.

features.label: Multi-provider agent supervision
features.description: Can it drive more than one coding-agent CLI/tool at once.

features.label: Coding agents supported
features.description: How many different coding agents (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor and so on) it can run, per its own docs.

features.label: Needs-you signal quality
features.description: How it tells you an agent is waiting on you, and how reliable that signal is.

features.label: Approve/deny a waiting permission prompt
features.description: Whether you can answer an agent's permission prompt from the manager itself.

features.label: Cross-provider delegation visible in one place
features.description: Handoffs between different providers/agents show up in one unified view.

features.label: Always-on assistant session
features.description: A persistent standing assistant session you can reach any time (not a task-bound worker).

features.label: Conversation (GUI) view of a session
features.description: A chat-style view of a session's plan/edits/results, as opposed to raw terminal text.

features.label: The real terminal of a session
features.description: Whether you can drop into the session's actual terminal.

features.label: Session organization
features.description: How sessions are grouped and browsed (list, worktrees, kanban, nested groups).

features.label: Prompt scratchpad with insert-not-send
features.description: A place to draft prompts and insert them into a session without immediately sending.

features.label: Saved prompt library
features.description: Reusable, saved prompts/actions you can fire with prior context pre-attached.

features.label: Built-in editors / browser
features.description: Ships its own code/markdown editors and/or an embedded browser.

features.label: Appearance control incl. host-terminal font
features.description: How much you can customize its look, including your actual terminal's font/settings.

features.label: Subscription usage HUD (from local logs)
features.description: Shows your subscription usage/limits, read from local logs rather than a fragile API endpoint.

features.label: Usage HUD with burn-rate + time-to-limit forecast
features.description: Predicts when you'll hit your usage limit, not just showing current usage.

features.label: Session-limit governor (park/resume at reset)
features.description: Automatically pauses work near a usage limit and resumes after the reset.

features.label: Account switch / hot-swap without re-login
features.description: Can switch between provider accounts without logging in again each time.

features.label: Personal-notes-vault task source
features.description: Can read your own personal notes vault (e.g. Obsidian) as its task queue, instead of only an issue tracker.

features.label: Issue-tracker / PR pipeline to merge
features.description: Integrates with GitHub/GitLab/Linear/Jira issues and pull requests.

features.label: Worktree management for agents
features.description: Manages isolated git worktrees per agent/task on your behalf.

features.label: Planner/orchestrator that splits and runs work
features.description: A higher-level agent that breaks a goal into sub-tasks and runs them.

features.label: Agent-to-agent messaging across sessions
features.description: Sessions or orchestrators can message each other directly.

features.label: Knowledge base agents can query
features.description: A notes/knowledge store agents can query before acting.

features.label: Native mobile app
features.description: A dedicated iOS/Android app, as opposed to reusing a terminal app.

features.label: Phone access without a new app/account
features.description: Can be reached from a phone using tools you already have, no new app or account.

features.label: Remote hosts (SSH)
features.description: Can drive or edit sessions on a remote machine over SSH.

features.label: Voice input
features.description: Can dictate to it by voice.

features.label: App shell
features.description: What the desktop/app UI is actually built on: Electron (with version, if pinned), Tauri 2, native, terminal UI, web app, or hosted cloud service.

features.label: Main languages
features.description: The top 2-3 languages in the project's own repo, from GitHub's language breakdown, with rough percentages.

features.label: Background process
features.description: Whether it runs a separate daemon/server process alongside the UI, and what it does, per its own source or docs.

features.label: Download size
features.description: The latest release's desktop installer size(s) per OS, from the release's own asset listing. Not a claim about how much it uses once running.

features.label: Memory weight vs Claude Desktop (estimate)
features.description: A labeled ESTIMATE, not a measurement: Claude Desktop is itself an Electron app, so this compares app shells only. Electron ~= about the same (heavier if it also runs a background daemon or several windows/an embedded terminal — the value says which); Tauri/system-WebView = lighter; terminal UI = much lighter; hosted service = cloud, local cost is a browser tab; unknown shell = not verified. The coding agents themselves (Claude Code, Codex, etc.) cost the same memory under every tool in this table — only the manager's own shell differs.

features.label: Runs inside a terminal you already have
features.description: Lives inside your existing terminal app, rather than shipping its own app/window.

features.label: License / cost
features.description: Open-source license, or commercial pricing model.

features.label: Extensibility for others (plugins/SDK)
features.description: Whether outside developers can extend it via a plugin or SDK surface.

features.label: Teams / multi-user
features.description: Built for more than one person to use together, as opposed to single-user.

features.label: Stability / maturity (honest)
features.description: How mature and stable it currently is, stated plainly.
